description: GROUPING_ID(e1, ..., en) returns the integer BIT-VECTOR for the current grouping set: e1 is the most significant bit, each ei is 1 when it is rolled up (aggregated over) and 0 when grouped by. Over ROLLUP(region, product) the detail rows are 0, the region subtotals 1 and the grand total 3. A single argument's bit is 1 exactly when that column's value is NULL. GROUPING_ID(a, b) equals GROUPING(a, b) for the same arguments. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupingIdTest (now retired); the Java counted rows by bitmask and, for the equality test, only compared the two columns to each other without pinning either - the converted test states both columns' VALUES, so a pair that agreed on the wrong number would fail.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, product VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT region, product, GROUPING_ID(region, product) AS grp FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region, product) ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, product NULLS LAST
CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, product VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT region, GROUPING_ID(region) AS gid FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region) ORDER BY region NULLS LAST
CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, product VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT region, product, GROUPING(region, product) AS g, GROUPING_ID(region, product) AS gid FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region, product) ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, product NULLS LAST
SELECT COUNT_IF(GROUPING(region, product) <> GROUPING_ID(region, product)) FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region, product)
